subject.declared_domain: NFRA_GLOBGRPH TO-F1 -- Kuzu query-surface provenance, and the CONTRACT OWNER for the sidecar suffixes and the Nessie HEAD oracle. Writes <db>._build_manifest.json beside each DB on a successful build for all three Kuzu loaders; supplies the provenance header kuzu_cli prints on EVERY comp-kuzu invocation; owns the FRESHGUARD leg-4 centralized marker stamp that all three graph writers call, and the _nessie_head_status BEHIND/CURRENT/UNKNOWN decision that _canonical's refresh trigger keys on.

as_of.graph_vintage: Holds no vintage of its own -- it is the thing that STAMPS and READS vintages. The marker it owns, s3://opal-313476888478-globgrph/warehouse/_branch_head.main.json, was measured live this session at LastModified 2026-08-30T02:11:47Z. The manifest it writes was measured beside the canonical DB at 902 B, ~14 min old at 03:35Z.

methodology.how: Three roles in one module. (1) MANIFEST: write_manifest stamps {schema_version, source_kind (tarball|nessie|stitch), source_vintage, built_at UTC ISO, node_count, edge_count} to a SIBLING path so it survives whether Kuzu materializes the DB as a file or a directory and a --force wipe cannot clobber it; read_manifest returns it or None. (2) HEAD ORACLE: read_branch_head_marker fetches the writer-stamped branch-head marker, and _nessie_head_status compares this DB's pinned nodes_snapshot_id against the marker's, as STRINGS because the marker carries int and the manifest carries str, returning 'current' | 'behind' | 'unknown' -- an absent marker yields UNKNOWN, explicitly never a silent guess, the mtime-scan oracle having been retired on CVO dc06744c6. (3) HEADER: format_provenance_header is a pure string builder (the caller decides the sink; kuzu_cli sends it to stderr so --json stays parseable) that surfaces a refresh failure LOUD at the top, distinguishes a DELIBERATE comp-kuzu-inc labeled-stale serve from a broken rebuild in different words, and prints a loud UNKNOWN VINTAGE block when no manifest exists.

Its writes happen on its callers' schedules: write_manifest on each successful loader build, stamp_marker on each of the three graph writers' commits (FRESHGUARD leg-4 makes it the SINGLE stamp all three call, because a triplicated stamp is the drift class that work fixed), and format_provenance_header on every comp-kuzu invocation.

persistence.form: Two JSON artifacts and one string. (a) <db>._build_manifest.json -- the per-DB build stamp, rewritten whole on each successful build. (b) warehouse/_branch_head.main.json -- the branch-head marker naming each table's metadata_location, snapshot_id and last_write_iso, with superseded versions archived under warehouse/_branch_head.history/. (c) the provenance header, a multi-line string returned to the caller rather than printed, so the module never chooses a sink.
persistence.evidence: Manifest schema documented :12-19 and written at :49-72; marker key :96 and history prefix :102; header returned as a joined string at the end of format_provenance_header (:545-641), with the docstring explicitly stating 'Pure string builder -- the caller decides where to write it'. Classified 'evidence' rather than 'source' or 'projection' ON PURPOSE: these artifacts are not the graph and are not derived from it as a view -- they are the CLAIMS ABOUT the graph's vintage that every consumer's freshness decision rests on, which is exactly what the evidence role names.

key.identity_space: TWO key spaces, joined by this module and not elsewhere. LOCAL: a DB path, from which every sidecar is derived by suffix. REMOTE: a fixed bucket-relative S3 key for the marker, plus per-table names inside it. The join between them is the snapshot_id comparison -- the manifest's pinned id (local, str) against the marker's HEAD id (remote, int).

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: MOSTLY EXEMPLARY, WITH ONE PRECISE EXCEPTION. read_manifest returns None when absent, and format_provenance_header turns that into a LOUD 'UNKNOWN VINTAGE' block rather than silence. _read_refresh_failure catches FileNotFoundError FIRST so ABSENT reads as healthy None, and returns {'kind': 'unreadable-marker'} for a present-but-corrupt marker so the header still fires -- its docstring names the incident that taught it (DS~B RAVC b50855e20: 'never let an unreadable marker read as a healthy None'). The header distinguishes a DELIBERATE comp-kuzu-inc labeled-stale serve from a genuinely broken rebuild in DIFFERENT WORDS, so a deliberate serve is never mislabeled. _nessie_head_status returns 'unknown' rather than guessing when the marker or its snapshot_id is missing. ⛔ THE EXCEPTION: read_branch_head_marker (:128-142) collapses FOUR different causes into one None -- an EMPTY BUCKET argument (:131-132), a boto3 IMPORT failure (:134-136), an S3 FETCH failure and a JSON PARSE failure (both :137-142, one bare except) -- and _nessie_head_status then renders that single value with the DETAIL STRING 'no branch-head marker' (:156), which asserts a specific cause it cannot know. The STATUS is honest ('unknown'); the DETAIL is not. ⛔ AND THE FUNCTION'S OWN DOCSTRING UNDERCOUNTS TOO: :130 says 'absent/unreachable/unparseable' -- THREE -- and omits the empty-bucket path entirely, so the documented contract is itself one cause short of the code.
silent_degrade_paths: read_branch_head_marker returns None on FOUR distinct causes (:131-132 empty bucket, :134-136 boto3 import, :137-142 fetch-or-parse), and :156 labels every one of them 'no branch-head marker' -- so a credentials failure, a truncated marker, or a caller that passed no bucket are all reported to the operator as a missing file, pointing the diagnosis at the wrong system
a boto3 IMPORT failure (:134-136) and an EMPTY BUCKET argument (:131-132) also return None, so a missing dependency and a caller bug are both reported as 'no branch-head marker'

the header degrades to fewer vintage lines, not an error, for an unrecognised source_kind -- benign, but a new loader kind would silently print less provenance rather than announcing that it is unhandled

I first wrote THREE in this card and corrected to FOUR after re-reading the function at source rather than from my note of it. _nessie_head_status :155-156 maps marker-is-None to ('unknown', 'no branch-head marker'). ⭐ THE CONTRAST IS THE FINDING AND IT IS INTERNAL TO THIS ONE FILE: _read_refresh_failure, 390 lines later, does exactly the right thing for the same class of question -- it catches FileNotFoundError FIRST to separate ABSENT from UNREADABLE, and its docstring says so explicitly. verdict.why: This is the contract owner the rest of the family leans on, and it mostly earns that position. It single-sources the sidecar suffixes so a writer and a reader cannot drift, and says why in the source. It refuses to guess a HEAD: an absent marker yields UNKNOWN, never a silent 'current', with the retired mtime oracle named and its CVO finding cited. It coerces int-vs-str at the snapshot-id comparison rather than leaving that trap to callers. It returns the provenance header as a string instead of choosing a sink, so --json output stays parseable while the header is still emitted on every comp-kuzu invocation -- though that emission is kuzu_cli's doing, not this module's: it returns a string and never prints, so 'provenance is always surfaced' is a property of the CALLER and is not guaranteed by the subject carded here. And _read_refresh_failure is the best failure reader on this face: FileNotFoundError caught FIRST so absent reads healthy, a corrupt marker returned as 'unreadable-marker' so the header still fires, with the incident that taught it named in the docstring. QUALIFIED, not SOUND, on one precise defect: read_branch_head_marker collapses FOUR causes -- empty-bucket, boto3-import, S3-fetch and JSON-parse -- into a single None, and _nessie_head_status then renders all four as the detail string 'no branch-head marker'; its own docstring lists three, undercounting its own code. The STATUS stays honest -- 'unknown' -- so nothing downstream is told the graph is current when it is not; but the CAUSE reported to a human is asserted rather than known, and it points the diagnosis at a missing file when the real fault may be credentials or corruption. The sharpest evidence that this is a defect rather than a design choice is 390 lines below in the same module: _read_refresh_failure separates ABSENT from UNREADABLE deliberately and explains why. The module already holds the lesson; one of its two sibling readers does not apply it.
